review_locator: PMCID:PMC11751857, The multifaceted role of XCL1 in health and disease; PMCID:PMC11621518, Molecular basis for chemokine recognition and activation of XCR1
primary_title: Structural and agonist properties of XCL2, the other member of the C-chemokine subfamily
decision_basis: The reviews identify XCL2 as the XCL1 paralog sharing XCR1; the cited primary study shows monomeric XCL2-dependent XCR1 calcium flux and chemotaxis, while the dimeric form preferentially binds glycosaminoglycans.
limitations_preserved: Preserve monomeric XCL2 as the GPCR-active form, dimeric XCL2/GAG binding as a separate state, and no CNS/SCI claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors; PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited
primary_title: Human monocyte chemoattractant protein (MCP)-4 signals through CCR2; Production of MCP-4 by airway cells and comparison of its biological activity
decision_basis: The reviews identify MCP-4/CCL13 as a CCR2 ligand; the cited primary studies show recombinant MCP-4 calcium signaling, CCR2b-transfectant migration and inhibition of MCP-1 binding.
limitations_preserved: Preserve CCR2B isoform and partial/shared MCP receptor pharmacology; primary evidence supports receptor-dependent activity without CNS/SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors; PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited
primary_title: Human MCP-4 is a novel CC chemokine signaling through CCR2 and CCR3; High expression of CCR3 in human blood basophils; Production of MCP-4 by airway cells
decision_basis: The reviews identify MCP-4/CCL13 as a CCR3 ligand; the cited primary studies show CCR3-transfectant or basophil/eosinophil CCR3-dependent calcium flux, chemotaxis and ligand competition.
limitations_preserved: Preserve MCP-4/CCR3 shared eotaxin-receptor and basophil/eosinophil context; no CNS/SCI transfer or exclusive CCR3 affinity claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7665155, CC Chemokines in a Tumor; PMCID:PMC3508751, CCL15 expression and implications
primary_title: Characterisation of macrophage inflammatory protein-5/HCC-2; Functional analysis of chemically synthesized CCL15 derivatives
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL15 as a CCR1 ligand; the cited primary studies show CCL15 binding to CCR1 and CCR1-dependent calcium/chemotaxis, with N-terminal truncation increasing activity.
limitations_preserved: Preserve full-length versus N-terminally truncated CCL15 processing and the stronger CCR1/weak CCR3 activity distinction; no CNS/SCI claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7665155, CC Chemokines in a Tumor; PMCID:PMC3508751, CCL15 expression and implications
primary_title: Characterisation of macrophage inflammatory protein-5/HCC-2; Functional analysis of chemically synthesized CCL15 derivatives
decision_basis: The reviews identify CCL15 as a lower-affinity CCR3 ligand; the cited primary studies show CCL15 competition at CCR3 and weak CCR3 calcium/chemotactic activity, especially for truncated forms.
limitations_preserved: Preserve weaker CCR3 efficacy, N-terminal processing and receptor-transfectant context; no CNS/SCI transfer or full-agonist equivalence claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors; PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited
primary_title: Eotaxin and monocyte chemotactic protein-3 use different modes of action
decision_basis: The reviews identify MCP-3/CCL7 as a CCR1 ligand; the cited primary study reports MCP-3 binding and monocyte activation through the CCR1/CCR2 receptor-selectivity context, with N-loop determinants for receptor usage.
limitations_preserved: Preserve MCP-3 N-loop/processing and promiscuous CCR1/CCR2/CCR3 pharmacology; no CNS/SCI transfer or unique receptor claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors; PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited
primary_title: Eotaxin and monocyte chemotactic protein-3 use different modes of action
decision_basis: The reviews identify MCP-3/CCL7 as a CCR2 ligand; the cited primary study supports MCP-3 receptor-selectivity and monocyte activation in the CCR1/CCR2/CCR3 context.
limitations_preserved: Preserve CCL7/MCP-3 as a shared/partial CCR2 ligand and retain receptor/isoform context; no CNS/SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors; PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited
primary_title: Eotaxin and monocyte chemotactic protein-3 use different modes of action; Chemokine receptor usage by human eosinophils
decision_basis: The reviews identify MCP-3/CCL7 as a CCR3 ligand; the cited primary studies support MCP-3 receptor recognition and CCR3-dependent eosinophil chemotaxis/calcium responses.
limitations_preserved: Preserve CCR3 shared-eotaxin pharmacology and receptor-blockade/eosinophil context; no CNS/SCI transfer or unique CCL7 receptor claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6120486, A guide to chemokines and their receptors; PMCID:PMC3396424, The Chemokine Superfamily Revisited
primary_title: CCR5 binds multiple CC-chemokines: MCP-3 acts as a natural antagonist
decision_basis: The reviews identify MCP-3/CCL7 as a non-signaling CCR5 ligand; the cited primary study demonstrates high-affinity MCP-3 binding to CCR5 without functional activation and inhibition of MIP-1beta-induced CCR5 responses.
limitations_preserved: Record as an inhibitory/non-signaling CCR5 edge, not productive activation; preserve high-affinity binding versus absent G-protein activation and no CNS/SCI claim.
